transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-04-22
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 min
Attendees: Ethan Park (Redwood AE), Marisol Chen (Redwood SE), Sanjay Rao (Willow - Head Cloud Eng), Ava Martinez (Willow - CISO), Derek Low (Willow - Compliance)
Recording ID: ff-20260422-willow-001

Auto-summary: quick discovery on residency + compliance. Customer wants to keep logs and any PII in regional control, evaluate Redwood Private or Dedicated with strict logging retention and KMS. Next: send security docs, schedule deep technical deep dive.

Transcript:
[00:00] Ethan: hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll kick off in a sec, i'm ethan from redwood inference, and with me is marisol our solutions engineer.
[00:09] Marisol: hi all, thanks for taking the time. sanjay, ava, derek, great to meet you.
[00:14] Sanjay: hey thanks, appreciate it. quick note we have a couple folks on mobile but should all be good.
[00:22] Ava: hi, ava here, ciso at willow, i'll focus on the compliance requirements.
[00:27] Derek: derek - compliance manager. i'll chime in on retention and audit.
[00:31] Ethan: great, objective for today is to understand your data residency and logging needs and figure out if hosted, dedicated, or private makes sense. also to surface any blockers for procurement.
[00:44] Sanjay: high level - we're a regional bank, we operate in US and EU, and certain product lines process health-like data and sensitive financial PII. we need to ensure EU workloads stay in eu region and logs for certain services can't leave the country.
[00:58] Marisol: got it. when you say logs can't leave the country, do you mean raw transcripts, model logs, or only aggregated metrics?
[01:05] Derek: primarily raw transcripts and request/response payloads that contain customer PII. we have rules that require those artifacts to remain on EU infrastructure and be encrypted with our keys.
[01:15] Ava: also retention: for fraud investigations we retain full logs for seven years, and audit trails must be immutable and discoverable.
[01:24] Ethan: ok that level of retention is heavy but understandable. Redwood supports multiple deployment modes; quick primer: Hosted API (fastest), Dedicated (reserved capacity with isolation), and Private (VPC or on-prem control plane). For EU-only constraints, Private or Dedicated deployed in an EU region are common patterns.
[01:45] Sanjay: a couple clarifying Qs: with Dedicated, do logs still flow through Redwood's central control plane, or can we keep logs in our VPC? we want to minimize any cross-border flow.
[01:58] Marisol: there are a couple variants - Dedicated can be set up in a customer VPC or in our hosted infra in an EU region. If you want full control of logs/KMS we recommend Private with the customer-managed control plane or on-prem. Dedicated hosted in eu still keeps compute and data in-region, but meta logs and analytics may be retained by redwood unless we configure log forwarding.
[02:22] Derek: that's the key. we need assurance that raw transcripts and request/response payloads never leave our boundary. encryption at rest and in transit with your certs isn't enough; we need our KMS and key ownership.
[02:35] Marisol: understood. Private (VPC) gives you control of key management using your KMS/HSM, and audit logs can be retained in your S3 in-region. We can sign an architecture doc that shows no request payloads leave the VPC.
[02:48] Ava: what about GDPR data subject requests? if an EU customer requests deletion, how do you ensure purge across caches, logs, and backups?
[02:58] Ethan: good question. our platform has a deletion workflow — we have prefixes and KV cache clearing. for Private you can run purge hooks inside your environment. For Hosted we can support deletion requests but some meta telemetry may be anonymized rather than fully deleted depending on retention policy — that's a subtlety we should surface.
[03:20] Sanjay: can you expand on telemetry vs raw payloads? we want telemetry for metrics but not the transcripts themselves.
[03:27] Marisol: telemetry = token counts, latency metrics, aggregate error rates. raw payloads = transcripts, inputs/outputs. We can route telemetry to Redwood while raw payloads remain in your storage. But Hosted often collects more meta by default; Dedicated/Private give more control.
[03:41] Derek: also need tamper-evident logs for auditors. do you support WORM or object lock on S3 and immutable event logs?
[03:50] Marisol: yes, in Private you can configure S3 object lock + immutable retention. We can also integrate with logging pipelines like Splunk or your SIEM via private forwarding.
[03:59] Ethan: adding to that, we can provide signed attestations and help with our SOC 2 artifact pack. we'll include those in the follow-up.
[04:07] Ava: HIPAA came up for one of our partners; do you have experience handling PHI?
[04:13] Ethan: Redwood has customers using the platform for regulated data, and while our Hosted offering can be used under BAA when configured, many customers choose Dedicated or Private for PHI so they control keys and audit trails. we will share our BAA baseline but legal review will be required.
[04:28] Sanjay: network: we prefer VPC peering or private link rather than public internet. can redwood support private connectivity to your endpoints?
[04:36] Marisol: yes — Private supports VPC peering, AWS PrivateLink, and on-prem connectors. Dedicated can also be deployed in your VPC. We'll need your network team to provide CIDR ranges and egress rules.
[04:47] Derek: one operational constraint — we mask account numbers in-transit and at rest. does Redwood provide auto-redaction or PII detection?
[04:56] Marisol: we have an optional PII redaction plugin; for high-risk data we recommend you run pre-processing in your environment before sending to Redwood, or use Private so the redaction step runs inside your VPC. There's also a configurable content filter in the pipeline.
[05:12] Ethan: on performance: a tradeoff — private/on-prem can increase latency vs Hosted, but Dedicated in-region often hits a good balance. what are your latency SLOs?
[05:21] Sanjay: for customer-facing chat features under 400ms median for short prompts, and up to 1s for longer generation is acceptable.
[05:28] Marisol: our benchmarks for in-region Dedicated show median token latency ~200-350ms depending on model and batch settings; we'll share a sample benchmark sheet.
[05:36] Ava: cost is a factor too; we want an estimate for reserved capacity and for hosted per token with EU region premium.
[05:44] Ethan: we'll prepare a pricing estimate for 3 reserved nodes and also a hosted fallback config; and show unit economics with batching and KV cache to reduce cost.
[05:53] Sanjay: on model updates — we need canary deploys and rollback if a model change causes regressions. do you support canary policies?
[05:59] Marisol: yes, Redwood has rollout controls — canary, A/B, automatic fallback to previous model variant. We'll show that in the deep dive. Sometimes the transcript has minor mislabels: 'canary' came across as 'kenary' in our notes.
[06:12] Derek: about logging retention again — seven years is long. backups are tricky. if backups are encrypted with your keys but stored outside region, that's a no-go.
[06:22] Marisol: with Private we can ensure backups are written to your in-region buckets only; with Dedicated we can configure retention and make sure backups adhere to your object lock policies.
[06:31] Ava: data subject access requests — we need proof of deletion. can you provide a deletion certificate or audit entry when a purge completes?
[06:40] Ethan: yes, for Private deployments we'll provide an audit event and you can ingest it into your SIEM. For Hosted we'll work to provide evidence but the mechanism differs; we'll include details in the security docs.
[06:51] Sanjay: any blockers on our side? our infra team is small, so the effort to stand up Private fully on-prem is a concern. what's the typical timeline and Redwood support model?
[07:02] Marisol: timeline depends — Dedicated in-customer-VPC can be 4-8 weeks, Private with customer-managed control plane or on-prem can be 8-16 weeks depending on approvals and network. Redwood provides an onboarding runbook, and we can assign a solutions engineer and a TAM for enterprise customers.
[07:20] Derek: procurement will ask about indemnity and data processing addendum — will redwood sign a DPA that covers data residency clauses?
[07:28] Ethan: we have a standard DPA that covers GDPR, and we can negotiate specific residency addenda for larger commitments. We'll flag legal to prepare a draft.
[07:36] Ava: one more: logging restrictions inside EU — do you maintain any support or troubleshooting access to raw logs? if we host everything in our VPC, will Redwood support still be able to help?
[07:47] Marisol: support can be granted via temporary, auditable access mechanisms (jumpbox, temporary IAM roles) under your control, or we can run diagnostics from logs you share. We try to minimize the need for Redwood to hold raw payloads.
[07:59] Sanjay: follow-up on key management: we use AWS KMS with HSM-backed CMKs. can you integrate with customer KMS keys for envelope encryption?
[08:09] Marisol: yes, envelope encryption with customer-managed keys is supported in Private and some Dedicated variants. We'll document the exact flow; sometimes there's a short-lived token exchange for the runtime to access keys under strict policy.
[08:21] Ethan: quick note — some names and acronyms might be off in this transcript, e.g., KV cache spelled as 'KV cash' in auto notes.
[08:29] Sanjay: haha noted.
[08:33] Derek: procurement question — do you have references for other banks or FS customers that did Private deployments?
[08:40] Ethan: yes we can share anonymized references and case studies; we'll include a short list in the follow-up.
[08:48] Ava: for HIPAA/PHI usage, you mentioned BAA baseline — do you have customers using Redwood in a BAA arrangement?
[08:56] Ethan: yes, there are customers with PHI under dedicated/private setups; we can provide our security pack and BAA terms as a starting point but legal review is required.
[09:06] Marisol: operational detail — when you do long-term retention, indexing for search and e-discovery matters. If you want immutable logs plus fast search we recommend a SIEM integration or a managed search index inside your region.
[09:19] Derek: ok. another technical item: are function/tool calls and tool outputs logged separately? we want to ensure external tool connectors don't leak data to third parties.
[09:31] Marisol: tool calling is configurable — connectors can run in your VPC and results stay in-region. We'll propose a hardened connector architecture.
[09:40] Sanjay: are there any features that are not possible with Private that are available on Hosted? e.g., streaming in the same way?
[09:47] Marisol: streaming is supported in Private too, but throughput tunings and autoscaling are more manual. Hosted gives automatic burst capacity. Dedicated offers reserved throughput plus burst options.
[09:58] Ethan: to recap, looks like Willow's must-haves: keep raw transcripts & PII in-region, KMS key ownership, immutable audit logs with 7-year retention, support for private connectivity, SIEM integration, and legal DPA + residency clauses.
[10:16] Ava: yes that's right. plus pricing and timeline info.
[10:20] Ethan: next steps are in the follow-up. We'll send SOC2/ISO pack, BAA baseline, architecture note for Private, pricing for 3-node Dedicated and hosted fallback, and schedule a technical deep dive.
[10:33] Sanjay: sounds good. any questions from our side?
[10:37] Derek: none right now, thanks.
[10:39] Ava: thanks, we'll review and come back with availability.
[10:42] Marisol: thanks all.
[10:43] Ethan: thanks everyone — we'll follow up with docs and times for the next call.
